_about: Editor decision (27 Sep 2026): judge p004 against '2 crore pucca houses by 2022', which official PRS figures show was met. Supersedes the p004 entry in 2026-09-27.json.

set.promise: Build 2 crore pucca houses for the poor by 2022 (PM Awas Yojana)

changes.why: Editor decision: measured as 2 crore pucca houses by 2022. PRS: 2.10 crore rural houses were completed under PMAY-G by 2022, before counting urban houses.

editorial.record: PRS Legislative Research: 2.10 crore rural pucca houses were completed under PMAY-Gramin by 2022; urban completions reached 68 lakh by January 2023.
editorial.summary: At the June 2015 launch of Housing for All, Prime Minister Narendra Modi cited a housing shortage of 2 crore units and said that by 2022 it was 'our responsibility to provide a house for everyone', in the PMO's account. Official figures compiled by PRS Legislative Research show 2.10 crore rural pucca houses completed under PMAY-Gramin by 2022, and 68 lakh urban houses by January 2023. The schemes' own targets, 2.95 crore rural houses and about 1.2 crore urban, were not reached by 2022; both were extended, and rural completions reached 2.61 crore by July 2024. The BJP's 2024 manifesto says more than 4 crore poor families have benefited.
editorial.promise_quote: Citing the existing housing shortage of 2 crore units, the Prime Minister said that India was completing 75 years of independence in 2022, and by then, it was our responsibility to provide a house for everyone.
